key_insight: Introduce Reflective Test-Time Planning: an approach that lets embodied LLM agents both deliberate during action selection and learn from each failed trial at test time, turning repeated mistakes into accumulated experience. This two-mode reflection (in-action and on-action) improves decision quality and sample efficiency without expensive offline retraining.
problem_solved: Embodied LLMs repeatedly make the same mistakes at deployment because they lack mechanisms to analyze failures and incorporate lessons on the fly.
method: Reflection-in-action: at test time, generate multiple candidate actions via scaled internal rollouts and score them to choose better immediate behavior.
Reflection-on-action: after each trial, analyze outcomes to identify failure modes, extract corrective heuristics or updated priors, and use them to bias future planning.
Integrate both modes into a test-time planning loop for embodied LLMs so the agent accumulates experience during deployment without offline retraining.
impact: Makes embodied agents more robust, sample-efficient, and safer in real-world deployment by enabling continuous, online learning from mistakes—useful for robotics, embodied simulation, and interactive AI systems.
visual_elements: Two-panel flow diagram: left 'Reflection-in-action' (multiple candidate rollouts → scoring → select action), right 'Reflection-on-action' (post-trial analysis → update priors/memory → next trial).
Before vs. After bar chart: success rate or error repetition frequency dropping after applying reflective planning.
Trajectory visualization: example robot attempt with candidate action overlays and final chosen path highlighted.
Icon set: robot + brain (LLM), checklist with X→check (failure→learning), clock/loop to indicate test-time iterative process.
paper_title: Learning from Trials and Errors: Reflective Test-Time Planning for Embodied LLMs
paper_authors: Yining Hong, Huang Huang, Manling Li, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu
